note.p: This is a page proof with Whitman's annotation about the poem's initial publication in the 5 January 1889 issue of the Critic. Retitled "To the Pending Year," the poem was later included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) and, as part of the "Good-Bye my Fancy" annex, in the so-called deathbed edition of Leaves of Grass (1891–1892).

lg.l:
Have I no weapon-word for thee—some message brief and
fierce?

Have I fought out and done indeed the battle? Is there no
shot left,
For all thy affectations, lisps, scorns, manifold silliness?
Nor for myself—my own rebellious self in thee?
Down, down, proud gorge!—though choking thee;
Thy bearded throat and high-borne forehead to the gutter;
Crouch low thy neck eleemosynary gifts.
